transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, well, the main reason I’m here is that at work... I'm a registered nurse, on the floor, and I just lose my train of thought constantly. Like, an IV pump will start beeping—which happens all the time, obviously. We actually just got these new pumps a few months ago and they are honestly so sensitive, like if a patient even slightly bends their arm it just screams at you. My coworker Sarah hates them, she actually was on the phone with clinical engineering for like twenty minutes yesterday because one wouldn't stop... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, sorry. So a pump beeps, or I hear someone asking another nurse a question down the hall, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was even working on. It's just happening all the time now.
Have you struggled with this kind of distractibility and forgetfulness since you were a child, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?

Um, no, it’s definitely been my whole life. Like, even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but really careless. I was constantly losing my worksheets or just completely forgetting to turn in my homework. 

I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable... she used to hand out these little foil star stickers, but only if your desk was clean on Fridays. Mine was always a disaster, just crammed full of crumpled papers. I actually found a bunch of old school supplies in my garage last weekend when I was trying to organize my camping gear. My husband and I are supposed to go up to the mountains next month, assuming the weather holds up. It rained the entire time we went last year and our tent leaked, which ruined my favorite sleeping bag... wait. Sorry. What did you ask me? 

Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, so because I was always losing my assignments, my mom literally had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night just to keep me on track. If she got up to check on dinner or something, I'd just completely drift off.
Growing up, did people often describe you as being constantly on the go, as if driven by a motor, or did you frequently struggle to stay seated when you were expected to?

Um, no, I never really had that problem. I didn't have trouble staying in my seat at all, and I wasn't bouncing off the walls or anything. In fact, I was usually too quiet. I’d just sit at my desk staring out the window, completely zoned out. 

I remember in fifth grade my desk was right next to the window, and there was this massive oak tree outside. I used to just watch the squirrels chasing each other around the branches for like, the entire math lesson. Squirrels are actually crazy aggressive, you know? I saw one pull a whole slice of pepperoni pizza out of a trash can at the park last week. It just dragged it right up the chain-link fence. My husband thought it was hilarious, he actually tried to take a video of it to send to his brother, because his brother is absolutely terrified of rodents. He got bit by a guinea pig when they were kids and it got super infected, so now he won't even go near the pet store... wait, what was the question? 

Oh, being on the go. Right. No, no one ever said I was driven by a motor. I was always pretty physically still, just... my mind was somewhere else.

In your daily work as a nurse, do you often make careless mistakes because you are not paying close enough attention to details, such as when you are documenting patient information or administering medications?

Um, yeah, unfortunately. It's really embarrassing, honestly. Like, I’ll be totally convinced I’ve finished an EHR audit or completely checked over a transfer note. But then my supervisor will pull me aside and point out that I completely missed a required field, or I put the wrong time down for a medication follow-up. Sometimes I'll even copy down the wrong room number, and I swear I looked right at it. 

Our charting system is just... it's a nightmare. They updated it last month and they moved all the tabs around, so the drop-down menu for the pain scale is where the vitals used to be. The other day, my friend Jessica—she works on the cardiac floor—she was complaining about the exact same thing. She actually ended up putting in a ticket with IT because her screen kept freezing every time she tried to log a new admission. IT is always so slow to respond, though. Like, last year my badge stopped swiping into the med room and it took them three days to issue me a new one. I had to keep asking the charge nurse to let me in, which was super annoying because she’s always so busy. She actually just had a baby, a little boy, and she brought him in to visit last week. He was wearing this tiny little knitted hat that looked like a strawberry... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? 

Oh, right, mistakes. Yeah, so I just miss details all the time, even when I think I'm being really careful. It's like I look at it, but my brain just doesn't register what I'm seeing.
In your daily life, do you find that you often act without thinking, or do you frequently find it difficult to wait your turn in conversations or social situations?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I act without thinking, and I definitely don't have trouble waiting my turn to talk. If anything, I'm usually the one listening because I kind of zone out while other people are talking. I definitely don't interrupt. 

My husband, though, he interrupts all the time. It drives my mom crazy. Like, we were at her house for dinner on Sunday—she made this incredible pot roast, which is weird because she usually only makes it for holidays, but she found a new recipe on Pinterest she wanted to try. She spends hours on Pinterest looking at recipes and home decor. She's been talking about redoing her guest bathroom for literally three years now. She wants to do this whole nautical theme with navy blue towels and a shower curtain with anchors on it, which I think is a little tacky, but I didn't say anything. I did see some cute little seashell soaps at Target the other day that would match perfectly, but the checkout line was so long I just put them back. Target has been so chaotic lately, they're remodeling the one near my house and the aisles are just a complete maze... 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about interrupting? 

Right, yeah. So no, I don't really do that. I'm pretty patient in conversations, I just... sometimes I forget what the conversation is even about while it's happening.
